speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your new movement disorder, could you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they started? Also, have you recently started or changed any psychiatric medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are these movements involuntary, such as stiffness or slow, writhing motions, and do they occur throughout the day? Have you noticed any muscle cramps in your neck or face, or difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: This sounds like akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. To confirm, does moving or pacing provide any temporary relief from that inner sense of restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming that; the relief with movement strongly supports akathisia. Since you've had no other medical history or substance use, I believe I have enough information. DIAGNOSIS READY: Antipsychotic-induced akathisia
